Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get operational proof that Redwood will not use AcmeCare customer interactions to improve or fine-tune models (we need a non-consuming/no-training commitment plus evidence of the controls). Specifically they asked for:

- A short attestation stating processed interactions are not used for model training or retention for improvement purposes;
- Proof of data export paths (SFTP logs or signed transfer receipts) showing we can route logs to our tenant SFTP or that you can retain evidence of deletion;
- An annotated DPA with your redlines so our legal team can reconcile clauses.

Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide and an ETA? If helpful, procurement can route DocuSign once we have the attestation template.

Best,

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 10:45 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> David, can you confirm the SFTP export scope and whether the runbook link is sufficient for procurement?

Hi all — quick technical note on what we can supply: 

- SFTP export logs: we can provide per-transfer manifests for the past 90 days for the tenant (job id, start/end timestamps, bytes transferred, sha256). These are generated by our transfer orchestrator and stored for audit.
- Deletion proof: we keep tombstone records for deleted objects with a signed deletion event (timestamp, operator id). We can produce a redacted sample set (no PII live data) as evidence.
- Non-consuming architecture: Redwood uses ephemeral KV and request-scoped buffers for hosted tenants; we never checkpoint tenant request content into model training pipelines unless a customer explicitly opts in via the console. I attach the internal runbook excerpt that maps request flow -> storage zones.

I've attached: sftp_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (fields we will include), and a short snippet exported as plain text used for attestation. If legal wants specific language for the attestation, drop it here and I'll sign off on the tech details.

-David
